terms.gloss: under age, not yet grown up; as a noun, a minor
terms.grammar: adjective, third declension, one ending; also impūbis, impūbe
evidence: Gai. Inst. 1.189: impūberēs quidem in tūtēlā esse (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Below the age of puberty, and so in law a minor, who must have a guardian, tūtor (Gai. Inst. 1.189, Lewis & Short). The form impūbēs is Cicero’s and Caesar’s; impūbis is Horace’s, Livy’s and Tacitus’s. Of age is pūbēs.

terms.gloss: under a given age (in law, under twenty-five)
terms.grammar: phrase: minor vīgintī quīnque annīs, or minor quam vīgintī quīnque annōrum
terms.comment: The lawyers’ phrase for those under twenty-five (the Digest’s title for them, 4.4: Dē minōribus vīgintī quīnque annīs); Morgan–Owens gives minor annīs, and major annīs for one of age.

terms.gloss: an orphan; a ward under a guardian
terms.comment: The child, fatherless, who is in a guardian’s care; feminine pūpilla.

phrases.latin: fīliumque ejus impūberem lēgātum ā patre missum in carcere necātum esse dīxit
phrases.english: and he said that his son, a boy under age sent by his father as an envoy, had been put to death in prison

sources: Lewis & Short: impubes · Lewis & Short: parvus · Lewis & Short: pupillus
Morgan–Owens, Adumbratio: s.v. minor; minor: legal adult; guardian: ward.
